facts.fact: DLA Piper states that the Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) came into force on 22 December 2023 and permits transfer of personal data outside Seychelles provided the transfer ensures an adequate level of protection, with appropriate safeguards or legal mechanisms.

note: No fact on the use aspect: the document names no list, model terms, procedure, guidance or application of the rule.
Treaty protocol clause on confidentiality of vessel data exchanged between the EU and Seychelles; states no national rule on sending data out of the country.
Trade agreement factsheet; the data localisation ban and digital trade line are a treaty matter, not a national rule on sending data abroad.
Meeting report on data protection cooperation and capacity building; says nothing of a rule on sending data abroad.
African Union Assembly urges all AfCFTA states to implement digital trade protocol commitments on cross-border data transfers; does not name Seychelles or state its rule.
Joint press release agreeing to explore cooperation on personal data protection; states no rule on sending data abroad.

facts.fact: The Commission received and handled 14 cases under the Act in 2025 (6 data transfers, 5 breaches, 2 refused deletion requests, 1 consultation), described as guidance, assessment and corrective advice, with no decision or sanction on a named controller and no count of cases settled.
